text:
The Jets were nine games without a win (0-7-2) and four goals down at Centre Bell when Tyrel Bauer, a sixth-round pick from 2020 playing for the Jets for the first time this season, scored the first NHL goal of his career with 2:39 left in regulation. Forty-two seconds later Morgan Barron made it 4-2, and Kyle Connor scored twice in the last 61 seconds, the second on a power play with 33 seconds left, to tie it. Dylan Samberg won it in overtime, 5-4, and ended the Canadiens' five-game winning streak.

The scoreboard hid how one-sided the game was. Winnipeg took 87 shot attempts to Montreal's 47 and put 47 on net to the Canadiens' 22, and our expected goals (a measure of chance quality) were 4.99 to 3.25. By our simulation of every shot, the Jets deserved to win 74 percent of the time. Montreal's lead came from efficiency: two power-play goals from Cole Caufield, the first on a 45 percent chance, and an early snap shot from Owen Beck on an 8 percent look. The Canadiens also blocked 23 shots to Winnipeg's nine. Jacob Fowler faced 47 shots and stopped 42, roughly what the chances called for.

For Winnipeg, the win ends a long skid and carries a small milestone, Adam Lowry's 300th career point on Samberg's winner. Connor was on the ice for 2.99 expected goals for and 0.42 against in nearly 28 minutes. Montreal had beaten the Jets 2-1 on Oct. 25 and arrived on a five-game run, so this loss stings, but their lead rested on thin chances, and that is worth watching.
